info.title: Resonance API
info.description: The versioned API for the native apps. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>` (the web uses its session cookie), or with an access token from POST /auth/exchange the same way. Additive changes only within v1.

get.summary: The signed-in account

post.summary: Onboarding: create your profile (an existing one comes back unchanged, unless it has no pen name yet)
post.description: A profile without a pen name — made before onboarding asked for one — takes the one sent (reserved, `409` when taken) with the region and writing language sent, keeping the rest; it then comes back `200`. Reaching anyone (a note, a message, a resonance that rings) takes a pen name.

200.description: Already had a profile (named now, if it had no pen name)

patch.summary: Change your pen name, bio, region, writing language, photo, translation languages or hint counts

get.summary: Whether a pen name is free

delete.summary: Empty your trash: every card in it is deleted for good, a page at a time
delete.description: The first call sends no `before`; call again with the answer's `before` while `remaining` and `deleted` are both above 0. Only cards still in the trash from before `before` are taken: one restored meanwhile, or moved there since, stays. `deleted` counts the cards this call deleted.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The first call's answer's `before` (ISO 8601); absent: now.

get.summary: One shelf of your card box
Several shelves of your card box at once
get.description: Each shelf asked for comes back exactly as `/me/cards?tab=` answers it; shelves not asked for are absent.

parameters.name: shelves
parameters.description: Shelves, comma-separated (e.g. `published,private,draft`): published, private, draft, resonated, linked, bookmarks, trash. Unknown names are ignored.

get.summary: Latest public cards, newest first (named cards of people you blocked are left out)
get.description: Anonymous cards come without a byline, and a block never leaves one out: that would name its author.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: A page's `nextCursor` (to the millisecond: cards sharing it can be skipped). Prefer `pageToken`.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: A page's `nextPageToken`: resumes exactly after its last card. Wins over `cursor`.

get.summary: Today's picks for you, each with the reason it was picked
get.description: Answers at once from the latest picks. While today's are being prepared `status` is `stale` (earlier picks, or a quick first pass without reasons); ask again a little later for `fresh` ones.

get.summary: Several cards at once, by slug or id, as list summaries (no story)
get.description: In the order asked, each card once; cards you may not read, named cards by someone you blocked, and unknown keys are left out. Anonymous cards come without a byline, and a block never leaves one out (nor any list or feed): that would name its author.

post.summary: Start a draft under the id your client made
post.description: The id is 20 letters and digits (as Firestore's auto ids), made by the client so an offline save can name the draft before it exists. Unpublished, its counters zeroed. Sent again for your own draft: `200` with `created: false`, nothing written. An id in use by another card, or one deleted for good, is `409 conflict`: make another. Anonymous and for connections only is `400 invalid_request` ("An anonymous card is public or private."). With `referenceCardId`, a card you may read (`404` otherwise), and not across a block unless it is anonymous (`403 blocked`). A cover is one of ours. Autosaves go to `PATCH /cards/{key}/draft`; publishing to `POST /cards/{key}/publish`.

get.summary: A card you may read, by slug or id, with its story
get.description: With `include`, the lists its page shows come along — each exactly what its own endpoint answers (`resonances`, `related`, `links`) — and `embeds`: the cards its story embeds. Someone else's 私人卡 (`visibility: private`, or `publishedAt: null`, with `isOwner: false`) is one its author sent you in a message: yours to read only — a note, a resonance or sending it on is refused as for any card you can't read — and only while that message stands (`GET /cards?keys=` answers it the same way).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The card slug, or (older cards) its id

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Lists to bring along, comma-separated (e.g. `resonances,related,links,embeds`): resonances, related, links, embeds. Unknown names are ignored.

patch.summary: Change your card's visibility and/or anonymity (only the fields sent)
patch.description: A published resonance made public under your name — published private, connections-only or anonymous, it reached no one — reaches the original's author after the response, as publishing it so would have: you two connected (not when the original is anonymous), their bell rung — once per reader and card, whatever path rang it first; never across a block, nor without a pen name. The answer never waits on it. One made private, connections-only or anonymous is at once no longer a reason you two are connected, and the connection goes when no reason is left (see `DELETE /cards/{key}/resonances/{cardId}`); the card still answers the original (listed under it while public, without your name when anonymous). An anonymous card is public or private: a change that would leave it anonymous and for connections only is `400 invalid_request` ("An anonymous card is public or private."); a card already that way stays so until either field changes. A card in the trash changes only by a restore: `409 conflict` ("This card is in the trash.").

200.description: The card as your card box shows it

delete.summary: Delete your card for good, draft or published (a retry after success is 404)
delete.description: Clients with a trash move cards there first (`POST /cards/{key}/trash`) and delete for good only from it, sending `onlyIfTrashed=true`: a card no longer in the trash (restored on another device) is then `409 conflict` ("This card is not in the trash.") and stays. A resonance is taken back with it, as `DELETE /cards/{key}/resonances/{cardId}` takes it back. The notes left on the card go with it. The only way a published card is deleted: a client may delete its own draft straight from Firestore, never a published card.

parameters.name: onlyIfTrashed
parameters.description: `true`: refuse (409) a card that is not in the trash.

post.summary: Move your card to the trash: private to everyone until you restore it, deleted for good after 30 days
post.description: Where a card goes when you delete it. While there it is private (nobody else can read, list or answer it: it is absent to them as a missing card is) and answers nothing (`referenceCardId` is parked); it keeps its slug, dates, story and place. A resonance is taken back at once, as hiding it is: no longer a reason you are connected, and the connection goes when no reason is left — restoring it never brings that back. The notes left on an anonymous card are deleted (they do not come back); a named card keeps its notes. It is changed by nothing but a restore (PATCH, publish, edits/apply and resonating with it are `409 conflict`, "This card is in the trash."). A card in the trash already is `changed: false`, its 30 days running from when it first went in. Someone else's card, or one past its purge date, is `404`.

post.summary: Bring your card back from the trash as it was (its visibility, slug and place)
post.description: A resonance answers its original again, as making a hidden one public again does — unless another of your cards answers that original now, or the original answers this card: then it comes back on its own (`droppedResonance`). Its original's author is rung only if this resonance never reached them before (once ever per reader and card). A card not in the trash is `changed: false`; one past its purge date (30 days in) is `404`.

get.summary: Public cards written in response to this one

post.summary: Make one of your published public cards a resonance of this one (connects you and rings its author, as publishing one does)
post.description: A card answers one card, and you answer a card with one of yours: `409 conflict` when the card already answers another, or another of your cards already answers this one — and when yours is in the trash ("This card is in the trash."). Asking again with the same card is `changed: false` and rings no one. An anonymous card connects no one and rings no one; an anonymous original rings its author but connects no one (that bell carries `payload.anonymous`: its push opens the card). A block either way is `403 blocked` for a named original; an anonymous one is answered all the same, and the block keeps it from reaching anyone. A card public under your name needs your pen name (`403 forbidden`). While it stands it is a reason you two are connected (one more, when you already are), and the original's author writing to you while it stands (a message, or a note in your thread) answers it: a reason for good. A letter waiting between you is left as it is — only its recipient answers it.

delete.summary: Your card stops answering this one and stays as a card of its own (204 whether or not it still did)
delete.description: It no longer keeps you connected with the card's author: the connection goes exactly when no reason is left — no other resonance between you either way, no answer to one from its original's author (their message or note in your thread while it stood; words from before it never answer it, and its writer's own answer nothing), no answered letter, no accepted invite, not made before reasons were kept. A letter waiting between you is left as it was. Their bell stays too: answering that card again rings and connects no one.

204.description: It no longer answers this card

get.summary: Whether your card was ever sent privately in a message — to warn before making it anonymous
get.description: True once one of your messages shared this card as a 私人卡, whatever became of the message since (unsent, stopped, the conversation deleted): its recipient may have read it, and knows it is yours. Making it anonymous is still yours to choose; clients say so first. Anyone else's card, or none, is `404`.

post.summary: You are reading this card: counts toward its readCount (204 whatever the card, and whether it counted)
post.description: Call it once the card page shows the card. The server counts each reader at most once per card per UTC day, never the card's author, and only a card you may read (published, not in the trash, public — or for connections only and you two connected; a named card across a block either way is not counted, an anonymous one is). The answer is always `204` for a well-formed id — it says nothing about the card — and the counting happens after it. Counted reads spend a daily budget; past it reads go uncounted, still `204`.

post.summary: How you read this card in one page view, as its running totals (204 whatever the card, and whether it was kept)
post.description: Send it when the card page is left or hidden (and again if it comes back and is left again): the `session` is the page view's own id, the numbers its totals so far — never deltas. The server keeps the largest each session has said and adds sessions up, so sending one twice counts once. Kept only for picking cards for you; the card's author hears at most a weekly count of three readers or more, never a name. Counted only for a card you may read and didn't write (published, not in the trash; a named card across a block either way is not counted, an anonymous one is). Numbers out of range are clamped. The answer is always `204` for a well-formed request — it says nothing about the card — and the keeping happens after it; past a daily budget, reports go unkept, still `204`.

put.summary: Resonate with a card (共振, the tap): its author is told once, ever, and your face shows to its readers
put.description: Checked in this order: the contract (`400`); your budget (`429`); the card (`404` for one you can't read, a draft, one in the trash, or someone else's 私人卡 shared with you in a conversation — a card is never resonated with on that pass); your own card (`400`); your pen name (`403 forbidden`, "Choose a pen name first."); a block either way on a named card (`403 blocked`). An anonymous card is answered exactly as without a block — its author just never hears of it. Its author is told after the answer, the first time only: a bell row and a push naming you (never across a block). A tap connects no one and lets the author write to no one. `changed: false` when you already resonated: nothing written, no one told. `409 conflict` is documented for a refusal to come; nothing answers it yet.

delete.summary: Take your resonance with a card back: it tells no one, and you leave its author's list and the faces at once
delete.description: Checked in this order: the contract (`400`); your budget (`429`); the card (`404` as for `tapCard`); your own card (`400`). It reaches no one: across a block too, and with no pen name. Resonating again tells its author nothing (once, ever). `changed: false` when there was nothing to take back. `403` and `409` are documented for refusals to come; nothing answers them yet.

put.summary: Say which part of a card stayed with you, after you resonated: one of its passages, or none (round 27)
put.description: Pick one of `CardDetail.tap.passages` (its `id`), or send `passage: null` to clear your pick. Since Wave 2 the card's readers see it as its author does — the sentence marked in the story with your face (`CardDetail.tap.picked`) and your row of who resonated (`TapPerson.passage`); read the card again to show it. Nothing rings and nothing is counted. Checked in this order: the contract (`400`); your budget (`429`, the tap's); the card (`404` wherever `CardDetail.tap` is null: one you can't read, a draft, one in the trash, your own, a named card across a block either way — an anonymous card is answered exactly as without a block); your tap on it is on (`409 conflict` otherwise: resonate first); the passage is one the card offers now (`400` otherwise — the options change when the story does: read the card again). Taking your tap back clears the pick.

get.summary: Who resonated with a card (共振), as you may see them
get.description: The card's author gets everyone, newest first, 30 a page (pass `nextPageToken` back as `pageToken`), each with the excerpt of the latest note they left on a named card (`note`; open your conversation with them) — never across a block, and never a note on an anonymous card. A reader (Wave 2) gets everyone they may see, the same pages: themselves first, then everyone else who resonated, minus anyone across a block with them (and on a named card with its author), each with their pick, never a note. `404` wherever `CardDetail.tap` is null. `429` is documented for a budget to come; nothing answers it yet. With `passage` (round 29; a reader's too since Wave 2), the pages hold only the people who picked that sentence (`CardDetail.tap.picked`), the same rows, order and page size.

parameters.name: passage
parameters.description: For the card's author: only the people who picked this sentence (a `TapPicked.id`). Ignored for a reader.

get.summary: A few recent cards sharing its tags

post.summary: Publish your card: stamps it once, gives it its slug, and lets a resonance reach its original
post.description: A resonance published public under your name reaches the original's author, the first time only: you two connected (not when the original is anonymous) and their bell rung — once per reader and card, whatever path rang it first; never across a block, nor without a pen name. A private, connections-only or anonymous one reaches no one. Either way the card is published: reaching out never fails it. An anonymous card is public or private: a draft set to be anonymous and for connections only is `400 invalid_request` ("An anonymous card is public or private.") and stays a draft. A card in the trash is `409 conflict` ("This card is in the trash.") until it is restored.

post.summary: A published public story translated by AI into the reader's interface language (title and story only)
post.description: For the card page's translate line: `to` is the interface language. Checked in this order: the contract (`400`); the card — one you may read, published and public (named or anonymous), not in the trash — else `404`, as for a card that is not there; a story over 30 000 characters is `413`; one already in that language (by its script: a Chinese story goes into English, a Latin-script one into 繁體中文, a Japanese or Korean one into either) `400`. A translation already made for the card as it is now is answered at once and spends nothing; otherwise your translation budget (`429`, 40 a day), then the model: `503` when it failed or ran out of time (nothing kept: ask again later). The answer says nothing about the author. Never cached.

post.summary: Apply your pending edit (cards/{id}/edits/current) to your published card, and clear it
post.description: An edit that makes a published resonance public under your name reaches the original's author after the response, as a PATCH doing so would (see updateCard); one that leaves it private, connections-only or anonymous takes it back, as that PATCH would. An edit that would leave the card anonymous and for connections only is `400 invalid_request` ("An anonymous card is public or private."), the card and the edit left as they were — unless the card already is so and the edit keeps both. A card in the trash is `409 conflict` ("This card is in the trash.").

patch.summary: Autosave your draft: only the fields sent, ordered by `rev`
patch.description: `rev` counts the client's saves of this draft, one higher each time. A save applies only when its `rev` is above the stored one (0 for a new draft); otherwise nothing changes and the answer is `200` with `applied: false` and the stored `rev` — a save that arrived late, or was sent twice, never overwrites newer words. A sent cover replaces the stored one whole (a `frame` left out is removed); `clear` removes the cover or the hue. The fields and limits are the rules' for a client writing its own card: anything else is `400`. A published card saves through its pending edit (`PUT /cards/{key}/edits/current`): `409 conflict`; a card in the trash is `409 conflict` ("This card is in the trash."); someone else's card is `404`. Each applied save is kept 7 days, to bring words back.

get.summary: Your working copy of your published card, or `edit: null`
get.description: Only yours: someone else's card is `404`. Checked each time (ETag → 304).

put.summary: Autosave your published card's working copy, whole, ordered by `rev`
put.description: Readers never see it until you apply it (`POST /cards/{key}/edits/apply`). Applied only when `rev` is above the stored copy's (else `200` with `applied: false`, as `PATCH …/draft`). It may keep a card anonymous and for connections only that already is, never make one so (`400 invalid_request`). A card in the trash is `409 conflict`.

delete.summary: Throw your working copy away (the live card is left as it was)

get.summary: Your whole thought map: nodes, arrows and groups
get.description: Yours alone. Cards by id only: what each is, `GET /cards?keys=` answers. Checked each time (ETag → 304).

post.summary: Change your thought map: a batch of ops, in order, all together
post.description: Every op applies, or none does: one the map never takes (an arrow from a card to itself) is `400` and changes nothing. An op on a node, arrow or group that is not there is skipped (its index in `skipped`), so a queue sent again or late does no harm. A group is made under the id the client chose.

post.summary: Report a card you can see (its author, anonymous or not, is filled in by the server)

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The card slug, or its id

post.summary: Report a person or a message sent to you (the server keeps a copy of what was reported)

get.summary: Cards linking to it (empty unless you wrote it)
A person's profile as you see it
get.description: With `include`, what `/cards` (its first page, of `limit` cards) and `/links` answer come along.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Lists to bring along, comma-separated (e.g. `cards,links`): cards, links. Unknown names are ignored.

get.summary: Their public cards, newest first (never anonymous ones)

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: A page's `nextCursor` (to the millisecond: cards sharing it can be skipped). Prefer `pageToken`.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: A page's `nextPageToken`: resumes exactly after its last card. Wins over `cursor`.

get.summary: Cards by others that link to theirs

post.summary: Accept a legacy invite sent to you: connects you two and rings its sender's bell (accepting again changes nothing); it answers a letter waiting between you
post.description: `409 conflict` once it is no longer open: declined, withdrawn, or past its `expiresAt` (it is closed as `expired` then, so inboxes should list only invites before their date). `403 forbidden` without a pen name; `403 blocked` across a block either way.

post.summary: Send a note to a card's author: rings them and lands in your conversation as a message (`kind: 'note'`, `cardRef` = the card). A note is a letter: it connects no one. Between two people not connected it waits in the conversation (`request: { from, cardId, at, count }`) until the author answers it with a message, which connects you (so does a note of theirs to you while yours waits); at most 3 unanswered in all, then 409 `conflict` ("Wait for them to reply."). Either of you may delete the conversation: the writer withdraws the letter, the author declines it, and it can no longer be answered — but the count of 3 is kept apart and goes only when it is answered. Only its recipient answers it: connected some other way (a resonance), it still waits, and the recipient's message or note clears it. On an anonymous card: the bell only (`payload.anonymous` true: its push opens the card — `data.route` `/card/{cardId}`, no `fromUserId` — and a bell list should open the card too, never a thread with the writer) — no conversation, no connection; across a block it is answered 201 all the same and delivered to no one (a refusal would name its author)
post.description: A `clientId` makes sending retry-safe: it becomes the note's id (and its message's in the thread), and the same one sent again (a retry after a lost answer) is answered `201` with that id as it was first sent, writing, counting and ringing nothing, while the note is there — whatever has become of the blocks or the card's visibility since. A card deleted takes its notes with it: a resend after that is `404`, as any note to a missing card is. Someone else's note, or a message already in the two people's thread on a named card, is `400` ("Not a valid client id.").

post.summary: Message someone you are connected with (opens the conversation; its first message rings their bell), or answer a note they left you while you weren't (`request.from` is them): that answer connects you — and answers it all the same once you are
post.description: Checked in this order: the contract (`400`); your message budget (`429`); the request itself (`400`: messaging yourself, no text, no card and no picture, a card and a picture together, a `clientId` or `replyTo` Firestore keeps for itself); `cardRef` (`404` for a card you can't read, or one in the trash; one of your own 私人卡, published or never, may be sent — the message is its recipient's pass to read it, never to answer it, for as long as the message stands and shares it (`stopSharingCard`) and the card is named and out of the trash, with no block either way; `400`, "An anonymous card is shared only while it is public.", for an anonymous card of yours no one else may read); a `clientId` already used — yours answers `201` as it was first sent, someone else's is `400`; your pen name (`403 forbidden`, "Choose a pen name first."); a block either way (`403 blocked`); the connection (`403 forbidden`, "You can message people you are connected with.", unless a letter of theirs waits in your conversation — then your answer connects you); `noteRef`, a note they left you on the card it names (else `400`, "That is not a note they left you."); `replyTo`, a message of this conversation (else `400`); `image`, a picture you uploaded for this conversation and sent with no other message (else `400`, "That is not a picture you can send here."). A reply to a note left on your anonymous card, or to a note no longer there whose card is gone too (deleting a card deletes its notes) or isn't yours, is sent without its `noteRef`, saying nothing of the card — and still answers a letter; a note no longer there on your own card, still there, is the `400`. A message from the original's author of a resonance standing between you, to its writer, answers that resonance (see `unresonateCard`).

get.summary: Your conversations, the most recently active first (50 a page)
get.description: What the `conversations` listener read: each with your unread count, the last message's preview, the letter it holds and the other person as their profile is now (`other: null` when their account is gone). Conversations with people you blocked are listed too, as before: filter them by your blocks. Ask again when `signals/{uid}` `inbox` moves, with `If-None-Match`: an unchanged list is `304`.

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: Conversation ids, comma-separated (1–20): only these of yours, the most recently active first, each with its person — one deleted, or not yours, is left out (no `nextPageToken`). For a client that knows which conversations moved (`signals/{uid}` `threads`) and holds the rest; without it, the first page as ever.

get.summary: A thread's messages, newest first
get.description: No cursor: the newest `limit` (the window to show, and to ask for again with `If-None-Match` when `signals/{uid}` `threads.{pair}` moves: a reaction, an unsend or a link preview changes it too). `before`: the page older than a message (`olderCursor`, or any message's `cursor`). `after`: the messages sent right after one (`newerCursor`), oldest of them first in time but answered newest first; `hasNewer` says the page was full. An open thread asks the window once with `changes=1`, then `after` its newest and `updatedAfter` its last answer's `updatedCursor`: what came and what changed (a reaction, an unsend, 停止分享), not the window again. Ordered by send time to the microsecond, then id: two messages sent in one millisecond are never skipped. `404` for anyone but its two participants, whether the conversation exists or not.

parameters.name: pair
parameters.description: The conversation's id: its two participants' uids, sorted, joined by `_`

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: A cursor: the page older than it

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: A cursor: what came after it (not with `before`)

parameters.name: updatedAfter
parameters.description: An answer's `updatedCursor`: also answer `updated`, the messages changed since it, of any age (not with `before`)

parameters.name: changes
parameters.description: `1`: answer an `updatedCursor` (implied by `updatedAfter`); an answer carrying one is never a 304

post.summary: You have read the thread: your unread count in it goes to 0
post.description: Nothing changes for the other person. `404` for anyone but its two participants, whether it exists or not.

parameters.name: pair
parameters.description: The conversation's id: its two participants' uids, sorted, joined by `_`

get.summary: Your bell, newest first (20 a page)
get.description: What the `notifications` listener read, each row's payload as the server wrote it (`anonymous` on a note or a resonance on one of your anonymous cards: open the card, never a thread), and the profiles of the people the rows name (a tap row's first 3 readers). Ask again when `signals/{uid}` `bell` moves, with `If-None-Match`. An open bell may ask the newest page once with `changes=1`, then `updatedAfter` its last answer's `updatedCursor`: only the rows changed since (`delta: true`: made, read, rung again), not the page again — or, when the server can't tell them all (a row went, too many changed, a cursor ten minutes old), the newest page whole.

parameters.name: updatedAfter
parameters.description: An answer's `updatedCursor`: only the rows changed since it, when the server can tell them all (not with `pageToken`)

post.summary: Mark bell rows of yours read: by id, or every one up to a time
post.description: Rows that aren't yours, and ids that name none, are ignored. A row read already keeps the time it was read.

get.summary: One of your conversations, as the list shows it
get.description: Its letter and your unread count, as the thread reads them. `404` for anyone but its two participants, whether it exists or not.

parameters.name: pair
parameters.description: The conversation's id: its two participants' uids, sorted, joined by `_`

delete.summary: Delete a conversation for both of its people: its messages, then the conversation (with a letter that waits in it — the writer withdraws it, its recipient declines it; the count of three unanswered notes is kept apart and stays). Either participant may; for anyone else it is `404`, whether the conversation exists or not. One already gone answers `204` (a retry after a lost answer)

parameters.name: pair
parameters.description: The conversation's id: its two participants' uids, sorted, joined by `_`

put.summary: Answer a message in your conversation with a reaction (one per person per message: a second replaces the first). Quiet: no bell, no push, no unread, the conversation list unchanged
put.description: Checked in this order: the contract (`400`); your reaction budget (`429`); the conversation and the message (`404` for one you are not in, or a message not in it, or unsent); your pen name (`403 forbidden`); a block either way (`403 blocked`); the connection (`403 forbidden` — a letter not yet answered takes no reactions). Your own messages take reactions too.

parameters.name: pair
parameters.description: The conversation's id: its two participants' uids, sorted, joined by `_`

delete.summary: Take your reaction to a message back. One already gone answers `204`

parameters.name: pair
parameters.description: The conversation's id: its two participants' uids, sorted, joined by `_`

post.summary: Unsend a message you sent, within 24 hours: for both of you it becomes a line saying it was unsent — its words, card, picture and link preview gone, quotes of it emptied. One already unsent answers `204`
post.description: Checked in this order: the contract (`400`); your unsend budget (`429`); the message (`404` unless it is yours, in this conversation); a note (`400`, "A note can't be unsent."); its age (`409 conflict`, "This message can no longer be unsent." past 24 hours). The server keeps what it said for 30 days, read only by moderation when the conversation is reported.

parameters.name: pair
parameters.description: The conversation's id: its two participants' uids, sorted, joined by `_`

delete.summary: Stop sharing your 私人卡 in this conversation (停止分享): every message of yours here that shares it stops being the other person's pass to read it — any time, not only within unsend's 24 hours. The messages stay; the card reads to them as one they cannot read. Sending it again shares it again. Nothing to stop answers `204`
delete.description: Checked in this order: the contract (`400`); your budget (`429`); the conversation (`404` for one you are not in, whether it exists or not). Across a block too: it reaches no one.

parameters.name: pair
parameters.description: The conversation's id: its two participants' uids, sorted, joined by `_`

204.description: No message here shares it any longer

post.summary: Upload a picture to send in a conversation (then send it: `sendMessage` with `image`)
post.description: The picture is kept upright, at most 2048 px on its longest side, as WebP without its metadata (place, camera); an animated GIF stays animated. Only the two people of the conversation can read it, once it is sent (`getChatImage`). Checked in this order: a request over 4 MB (`400`); the form (`400`: no file, a file over 4 MB, a `to` or `clientId` that is not one); a `clientId` already used — yours answers `201` as it was first uploaded, spending nothing; someone else's is `400`; your picture budget (`429`); your pen name (`403 forbidden`); a block either way (`403 blocked`); whether you may message `to` at all (`403 forbidden`, as `sendMessage` says it); the picture itself (`400`: not a JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF, or more than 50 megapixels). A picture never sent is deleted after a day.

file.description: JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF, at most 4 MB

clientId.description: The sender's own id for this picture (16–64 of A–Z a–z 0–9 _ -), kept for every retry: it becomes the picture's id, so uploading it again after a lost answer finds the one already kept

get.summary: A picture sent in one of your conversations
get.description: For the two people of its conversation, while the message that carries it is there (a deleted conversation takes its pictures with it); `404` for anything else, never saying why. The bytes never change: keep them.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: `thumb`: at most 960 px on its longest side, for the thread; `full` (the default): as kept

get.summary: Which pushes this account wants
get.description: `picks` and `connectionCards` are off until turned on; `messages` (messages and notes) is on until turned off (an account that never set them reads those two off and messages on).

patch.summary: Turn "a card for tonight", "new cards from your connections" or message pushes on or off
patch.description: Only the switches sent change (`null` or absent leaves one as it is); turning one on records when. Answers the settings as they are now. Ask for the OS permission before turning one on: the server cannot tell whether this install may show notifications.

put.summary: Register this install's push token (it moves to you if someone else was signed in on it)

parameters.name: installationId
parameters.description: The install's own stable id (8–128 of A–Z a–z 0–9 _ . : -)

delete.summary: On sign-out: stop pushing to this install

get.summary: What an app asks at launch: the builds that must or should update, and which paths to take
get.description: No sign-in needed; the same for everyone (`Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=60`, an `ETag`, `304` on a match). A build below `minBuild` for its platform shows the update screen and goes no further; one below `recommendedBuild` may say an update is waiting. `features`: each flag true takes the /api/v1 path, false the older one.

get.summary: Profiles by id, at most 30, in the order asked
get.description: Each id once, in the order asked; an account that is gone (deleted, or never was) comes back `gone` with nothing else. A profile is public: a block changes nothing here. `429` past the hourly budget.

put.summary: Bookmark a card you may read (again: unchanged)
put.description: `404` for a card you may not read, exactly as GET /cards/{key} answers it. Your bookmarks are yours alone: no one is told.

delete.summary: Take a bookmark back (whether or not there was one)

get.summary: Everyone you blocked, the latest first

put.summary: Block someone: the connection ends and every pending invite between you is withdrawn, at once
put.description: They are never told. Blocking again changes nothing; yourself is `400`.

delete.summary: Unblock someone: only the block goes (a connection it ended stays ended)

get.summary: The people you are connected with, the latest first
get.description: Ask again when `signals/{uid}` `graph` moves (every connection made or ended moves both people's), with `If-None-Match`.

get.summary: Legacy invites waiting for your answer (pending and before their date), the latest first

post.summary: Say no to a legacy invite sent to you: it closes, and no one is told (again: unchanged)
post.description: `404` for an invite that is not yours to answer; `409` once it closed otherwise (accepted, withdrawn, expired).

post.summary: Trade a sign-in at the identity provider (a Firebase ID token) for Resonance's own tokens
post.description: The token is checked as a write would check it (a disabled or revoked account is `401`). Answers a short-lived access token — sent as the bearer credential, where a Firebase ID token is sent today; both are accepted — and a refresh token. `userId` is the account id the sign-in always had. `503` where sessions are not enabled: keep sending the Firebase ID token. `429` past the hourly budget.

post.summary: Trade a refresh token for the next access and refresh tokens (each refresh token is good once)
post.description: A refresh token presented again within 30 seconds of its use, while the token it was traded for is still unused, is the client's own second try (two refreshes racing, a retry after a lost answer): `409` `conflict`, nothing revoked and no tokens handed out — use the pair the other request got, or, holding none, log this token out and exchange again. Presented again otherwise it is taken for stolen: the account is signed out everywhere (every session, the Firebase sign-in too) and this answers `401` (sign in again, then exchange). So does an account deleted, disabled or signed out everywhere since. `503` where sessions are not enabled.

post.summary: End this device's session: its refresh token, and every one rotated from the same exchange, revoked
post.description: The access token already handed out stands until it expires (at most 15 minutes). An unknown token answers the same.

ApiError.description: Every non-2xx response has this shape.

AccountDeletionStatus.description: A scheduled deletion of the account (what GET /api/account/deletion answers as `deletion`).

CoverFrame.description: Where a cover is looked at: every shape it is drawn in centres its own crop on (cx, cy) at `zoom`, moved to lie inside the picture (coverCrop, pinned by native/fixtures/cover-frame.json). Null or absent: the centre at zoom 1.

SummaryTranslation.description: A card's title and excerpt translated by AI into one interface language.

SummaryTranslations.description: A published public card's title and excerpt translated by AI, made when it was published or last edited: into English for a Chinese story, into 繁體中文 for a Latin-script one, both for Japanese or Korean. Sent only while they still describe the card as it is. Show one only when the reader turned auto-translate on, and mark it.

CardBox.description: Shelves of your card box, each one asked for (and only those) exactly as GET /me/cards?tab= answers it.

status.description: fresh: today's picks. stale: earlier (or quick, reason-less) picks while today's are prepared; ask again later. Absent: fresh.

RecommendedFeed.description: Today's picks (a CardList, plus whether they are today's).

image.description: A site-relative path ('/api/link-image?u=…&s=…'): resolve it against the API's origin. Null when the page had no picture.

LinkPreview.description: What a link says about itself: the title, description, site name and picture of its page, as the server read it.

TapPassage.description: One passage a card offers after you resonate with it (round 27): the author's own words, picked when it was published.

TapPicked.description: A sentence of the author's story that readers picked after they resonated, and the faces of who picked it (round 29; every reader sees them since Wave 2).

CardTap.description: The resonance tap (共振) on a card: whether you resonated, and the faces of who did as you may see them.

linkPreviews.description: Previews of the links standing alone in the story, in reading order (at most 10). Draw such a paragraph as a link card when its normalized URL has a preview here, else as the plain link. Absent from older servers.

CreateProfileRequest.description: Onboarding: the pen name, region and writing language of a new account.

UpdateCardRequest.description: Your card's visibility and byline; only the fields sent change.

TranslationResponse.description: A story translated by AI into the reader's interface language (title and story only).

ResonateRequest.description: Make a card you have already written a resonance of this one.

TapList.description: Who resonated with a card (共振): everyone you may see, for its author and for a reader alike (a reader: themselves first; notes for the author alone).

ReadingReportRequest.description: How a reader read a card in one page view, as the session's running totals so far (send it again as they grow).

SendNoteRequest.description: A note to a card's author (the server finds the author — anonymous cards too).

StickerRef.description: A 小紙團 sticker: its pack and its id in the pack (public/stickers/catalog.json).

AlbumRef.description: Several pictures sent together: the album, this picture's place in it, and how many it has.

ChatImageResponse.description: A picture uploaded for a conversation, ready to be sent in a message.

RegisterDeviceRequest.description: This install's push token. Register after sign-in and whenever the token, the app's language or the time zone changes.

NotificationSettings.description: Which pushes you want. picks and connectionCards go beyond the ones answering you and are off until turned on; messages (messages and notes) and resonanceTaps (someone resonated with your card) are on until turned off. A card answering yours always rings.

UpdateNotificationSettingsRequest.description: Only the switches sent change; turning one on records when you agreed to it.

ReportCardRequest.description: Report a card — anonymous ones too: the server knows its author, the app doesn't.

CreateReportRequest.description: Report a person or a message. The server keeps a copy of what was reported, so deleting it later erases no evidence.

SetReactionRequest.description: Answer a message with a reaction (it replaces your own earlier one on that message).

PrivateShares.description: Whether your card was ever sent privately in a message (a 私人卡 shared in a conversation). Its recipient knows you wrote it, so making it anonymous hides it from no one who read it then.

HandleAvailability.description: Whether a pen name is free (your own counts as free).

ClientBuilds.description: A build number per app (iOS CFBundleVersion, Android versionCode).

ClientFeatures.description: Which paths an app build takes: the /api/v1 path when true, its older Firestore path when false (the server's rollback).

ClientConfig.description: What the apps ask at launch (GET /client-config, no sign-in needed): the builds they need, and which paths to take.

Person.description: A profile by its id, as anyone may read it.

PersonList.description: The people asked for, in the order asked, each once.

BlockList.description: Everyone you blocked, the latest first.

ConnectionList.description: The people you are connected with, the latest first.

InviteList.description: Legacy invites waiting for your answer, the latest first.

MapNode.description: A card placed on your thought map. Only its id: what the card is, `GET /cards?keys=` answers as for any card.

MapEdge.description: An arrow between two cards on your map, with its words.

MapGroup.description: A titled region of your map that files the cards inside it.

ThoughtMap.description: Your whole thought map (yours alone: no one else can read it). Numbers a stored item lacks read as the clients read them: x, y 0; a group's hue 55, w 320, h 240.

MapOp.description: One change to your thought map, named by `op`, with that op's fields only (a null field is absent): addNode {cardId, x, y} places a card (again: written whole, unfiled); moveNode {cardId, x, y, groupId?} moves it (and files it when groupId is sent); setNodeGroup {cardId, groupId?} files or unfiles it; removeNode {cardId} takes it off with every arrow touching it; addEdge {sourceCardId, targetCardId, label?} draws an arrow (never to itself; id `{source}_{target}`); setEdgeLabel {id, label}; removeEdge {id}; addGroup {groupId, title, hue, x, y, w, h} under the id the client chose; updateGroup {groupId, …the fields that change}; removeGroup {groupId} (its cards stay, unfiled). Ids are 1–128 characters, labels and titles at most 500. A change to a node, arrow or group that is not there (any more) is skipped.

MapOpsRequest.description: Up to 200 changes, applied in order and all together (none when one is refused).

DraftMedia.description: A cover as a draft or a pending edit keeps it. Sent, it replaces the cover whole: a field left out or null (a `frame`, a `thumbUrl`) is gone from it.

CreateDraftRequest.description: A new draft under the id the client made. Anonymous and for connections only is refused (`400`).

UpdateDraftRequest.description: Only the fields sent change; a field that is null or absent is left as it is.

PendingEditRequest.description: The whole working copy of your published card, replacing the one kept (never merged).

PendingEdit.description: Your unsaved working copy of a published card (`edits/current`).

PendingEditBox.description: Your pending edit of the card, or null when there is none.

DeletedPendingEdit.description: False when there was none to delete.

ConversationLastMessage.description: The conversation list's preview of the last message.

ConversationLetter.description: The letter a conversation holds: notes left by someone not connected, waiting for an answer.

Conversation.description: One of your conversations, as the list shows it.

ConversationList.description: Your conversations, the most recently active first, 50 a page.

MessageQuote.description: A reply's snapshot of the message it answers.

ThreadMessage.description: A message as the thread shows it, its fields as stored.

MessagePage.description: A page of a thread's messages.

BellPayload.description: What a bell row says, as the server wrote it (the fields the clients draw).

MarkNotificationsReadRequest.description: Mark bell rows read: by id, or everything up to a time.

AuthExchangeRequest.description: A sign-in at the identity provider, traded for Resonance's own tokens.

AuthRefreshRequest.description: A refresh token, traded (once) for the next pair — or, to log out, revoked.

AuthSession.description: Resonance's own session: a short-lived access token and the refresh token for the next one.
